summary.intent: Execute all plans in Phase 60 (IPNS Verification Cross-Layer Closeout) using wave-based sequential subagent execution, hardening IPNS verification to be strict fail-closed across Rust and TypeScript layers.
summary.outcome: Wave 1 plans 60-01 and 60-02 completed successfully (Rust verify chokepoint relocated/hardened, all 9 first-publish producers unified to seq=1); 60-03 was in-flight at transcript end. The phase was ~2/8 plans complete.

repo: Phase 60 has 8 plans across 4 waves; Wave 4 (60-08) is non-autonomous (staging wipe + redeploy) requiring a human checkpoint.
The project uses worktree isolation per plan but the GSD harness cannot reliably merge back isolation=worktree agent branches, so sequential execution on the main feature branch was chosen instead.
No project-specific executor skills payload exists (gsd-tools query returns empty).
All 9 first-publish IPNS producers span FUSE, desktop Tauri, sdk-core, and web — a cross-layer dependency that Wave 1 (60-02) unified to seq=1.
Pre-existing dead-code warnings exist in vendored `fuser` crate and a test mock; these are noise, not regressions.
The VerifyError::Legacy variant was fully removed by 60-01 — all 9 FUSE caller arms were folded to Invalid, despite 60-04 being declared the consumer migration wave.

code.finding: Previously referenced VerifyError::Legacy; after 60-01 this arm was folded to VerifyError::Invalid. The E0599 compile error seen mid-run was a stale mid-edit snapshot, not a real failure.
Destination for the relocated verified-IPNS-resolve implementation moved from crates/fuse/src/verify.rs so sdk/fuse/desktop share one implementation.

workflow: When worktree merge-back is unreliable, sequential subagent execution on the main branch is the correct fallback — trades wall-clock for correctness.
Mid-execution compile error diagnostics can be stale snapshots from mid-edit state; always run cargo check authoritatively before marking a plan failed.
Wave-based execution requires a build gate between waves to catch cross-plan breakage before proceeding.

friction: 60-01 executor reported a compile error (metadata.rs:619 VerifyError::Legacy E0599) that turned out to be a stale mid-edit snapshot, requiring an extra manual cargo check round-trip to confirm the tree was actually green.

60-04 was declared the wave-2 FUSE consumer migration plan, but 60-01 already folded all 9 arms — scope boundary between plans was blurry, requiring post-hoc grep verification to confirm no double-work or missed sites.
The GSD worktree merge-back limitation forced sequential execution, eliminating the parallelism benefit of wave-based dispatch for this phase.
